1. Case 1: USP9X-related syndromic CHA
This 3-month-old infant had nasal obstruction, failure to thrive, craniosynostosis, frontal bossing, and limb abnormalities. Examination showed membranous choanal atresia with perforations; 3D CT excluded bony atresia. A de novo USP9X mutation explains the multisystem phenotype and directly supports USP9X-related syndromic choanal atresia. Isolated and acquired causes are excluded by syndromic features, congenital findings, and genetic evidence. Alternative causes are unlikely. Frontier sufficient.

Here is the reference diagnosis for this case:
1. Case 1: Choanal atresia with USP9X gene mutation
